title: Count Valid Paths in a Tree
summary: Given an undirected tree with n nodes numbered 1 to n, and a 2D array of edges, calculate the count of valid paths.
statement: Given an undirected tree with n nodes numbered 1 to n, and a 2D array of edges, calculate the count of valid paths. A path is valid if exactly one node label in the path is a prime number. A path is a sequence of distinct nodes connected by edges, and (a, b) and (b, a) are considered the same path.
constraints: Nodes are labeled 1 through n and edges form an undirected tree.
Count unordered endpoint pairs whose complete path contains exactly one prime-labeled node.
hints: Removing prime nodes splits the tree into nonprime components; a valid path chooses one prime and endpoints in at most two adjacent components or at the prime.
Label nonprime components and accumulate their sizes around each prime.
For each adjacent size, add size for prime-to-component paths and size*previous_total for cross-component paths.
Any path with exactly one prime decomposes uniquely this way, and combining two different adjacent components cannot introduce another prime.
editorial: Any path with exactly one prime decomposes uniquely this way, and combining two different adjacent components cannot introduce another prime.

tests.explanation: The four qualifying endpoint pairs each pass through exactly one of nodes two or three.
Nonprime components adjacent to each prime determine all valid cross-component pairs.
